candidates.name: Mask-Normalized Chirplet Routing and Synthesis
build_steps: Represent each identity track as timestamped joint angles, bone vectors, and confidence-weighted motion channels; retain an explicit observation mask rather than interpolating missing joints.
Split tracks into 128-frame windows with 75% overlap and apply a shared complex chirplet bank spanning log-period and within-window chirp-rate bins.
Normalize every complex convolution by the mask-window energy, and discard coefficients whose effective support falls below a fixed threshold.

Derive local tempo posterior, chirp slope, spectral concentration, and phase from the coefficients; use these quantities to route each window among shared learned response experts while keeping recurrent state private to the identity.

Train without per-person count or period targets using temporal-resampling equivariance, masked pose reconstruction, cross-augmentation phase consistency, overlap phase consistency, and expert-load regularization.

Synthesize one periodicity response per identity with squared-window normalized overlap-add; decode once using phase-supported peaks inside a half-open valid-support interval, with reflected context used only for feature computation and never counted.
candidates.hypothesis: A chirplet representation that models local frequency slope will preserve cycle evidence during within-track acceleration and deceleration better than track-global spectral features or stationary local Fourier bins, while mask normalization and phase-consistent synthesis will prevent missing poses and window seams from becoming false cycles.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Freeze a checksummed MultiRep release and canonical-source mapping; split by source video so no person crop, augmentation, or neighboring segment crosses train, development, and test partitions. Use supplied/oracle tracks to isolate counting, and disclose all external pose supervision.
comparisons: Local stationary STFT with uniform routing
Same chirplet model with hard routing
Window-count summation instead of response synthesis
diagnostics: Piecewise linear and piecewise quadratic time warps applied only after splitting
Random joint dropout, contiguous frame gaps, and timestamp jitter
Plots of local period, chirp-rate posterior, routing entropy, phase, synthesized response, and clean-to-corrupt degradation
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.evaluation: Three seeds; Period-mAP, AP50, AP75, AvgMAE, AvgOBO; paired video-cluster bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.

success: At least 2.0 absolute Period-mAP points and 8% relative AvgMAE improvement over track-global tempo on the frozen piecewise-warp diagnostic.
At least 30% lower clean-to-warp degradation than stationary local STFT.
Median overlap phase discontinuity at most 0.25 rad and seam-adjacent false-peak rate below 3%.
Paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval excludes zero for the primary AvgMAE difference.
failure: Less than 1.0 absolute Period-mAP improvement and less than 3% relative AvgMAE improvement over track-global tempo.
Masked corruption causes more than 15% additional AvgMAE at 20% missing frames.
Removing chirp-rate bins changes AvgMAE by less than 1%, indicating that the nonstationary component is unused.
More than 5% of decoded peaks occur within one decoder suppression radius of an overlap seam.

candidates.risk: Chirplet slope may follow camera or limb-specific motion rather than repetition tempo; self-supervised phase losses can admit harmonics or phase-reversed solutions.

engineer_gpu_effort.engineering: High: custom complex masked convolution, stable chirplet parameterization, synthesis tests, and seam instrumentation; approximately 4-6 engineer-weeks.
engineer_gpu_effort.gpu: Moderate: 3 seeds plus ablations on 2-4 GPUs; expected 300-600 GPU-hours after pose extraction.

unavailable_inputs: A leakage-free checksummed MultiRep release and canonical-source split
Verified supplied-track annotations aligned to pose timestamps
Frozen evaluation code for Period-mAP and count metrics
Raw videos or pose detections for the chosen release if they are not locally licensed
closest_priors: Runia et al. 2018 nonstationary temporal wavelet filtering
RepNet per-frame period and periodicity prediction
PAMS period-adaptive skeleton counting and speed-variation tests
candidates.why_it_matters: It tests whether explicitly estimating tempo slope inside each person's trajectory, rather than selecting a scale from a stationary spectrum, improves counting under acceleration, deceleration, and partial observation.

candidates.name: Irregular-Time Lomb Phase Counting
build_steps: Keep original timestamps and confidence masks for every pose channel; do not fill dropped frames before tempo estimation.

In each overlapping identity window, fit confidence-weighted sine and cosine bases on a log-frequency grid using generalized Lomb-Scargle least squares; obtain complex coefficients and their covariance from the weighted normal equations.
Pool joint-wise spectra with learned reliability weights and infer a local frequency posterior, periodicity probability, phase, and phase variance.
Feed the complex coefficients and uncertainty to shared tempo-conditioned response experts, with identity-private hidden state carried only across windows from the same track.
Train with masked-sample prediction, invariance to synthetic frame dropping, known timestamp-jitter consistency, and overlap agreement of complex phase and periodicity response.

Reconstruct response values only over observed support using uncertainty-weighted normalized overlap-add; during long gaps, propagate a phase distribution but suppress integer-cycle commitments unless posterior variance stays below a preregistered bound.
candidates.hypothesis: Direct irregular-time estimation will be more stable than interpolation followed by STFT when pose tracks contain dropped frames, variable frame intervals, or short occlusions, and phase covariance will identify intervals where count decisions should be deferred.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Use a frozen source-video-disjoint MultiRep split with supplied tracks. Generate all missing-frame and timestamp-jitter variants online from each already-assigned split, recording corruption seeds and never selecting corruption parameters on test.
comparisons: Mask-channel neural encoder without irregular-time spectral estimation
diagnostics: Independent random frame loss at 10%, 20%, and 40%
Contiguous gaps of 0.25, 0.5, and 1.0 estimated local cycles
Timestamp jitter at 5% and 15% of median frame interval
Error stratified by effective observations per cycle
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.evaluation: Three seeds; standard MRAC metrics plus gap-local false-cycle rate, phase calibration, and paired video-cluster bootstrap intervals.

success: At 20% frame loss, relative AvgMAE degradation is at least 35% smaller than interpolation plus STFT.
For gaps up to 0.5 local cycles, gap-local false-cycle rate is below 5%.
Phase-error 90% intervals cover 85%-95% of held-out synthetic phase perturbations.
Clean-data AvgMAE is no more than 3% worse than the strongest regular-sampling comparison.
failure: At 20% frame loss, AvgMAE differs by less than 3% from interpolation plus STFT.
The model commits more than 0.15 expected cycles per fully unobserved 0.5-cycle gap.
Covariance is uncalibrated, with 90% phase intervals covering below 75% or above 99%.
Weighted least-squares failures or ill-conditioning affect more than 1% of evaluated windows.

candidates.risk: Lomb-Scargle assumes locally sinusoidal channels and can lock onto limb harmonics; per-window matrix solves may be numerically unstable under structured occlusion.

engineer_gpu_effort.engineering: Medium-high: batched differentiable weighted solves, covariance propagation, and gap-aware decoding; approximately 3-5 engineer-weeks.
engineer_gpu_effort.gpu: Low-moderate: spectral solves add compute but require no large backbone; approximately 200-400 GPU-hours for three seeds and corruptions.

unavailable_inputs: Exact frame timestamps for MultiRep videos
Pose confidence or joint-visibility values rather than only interpolated coordinates
Leakage-free MultiRep provenance and split checksum
Ground-truth timing needed solely to validate synthetic phase uncertainty, if no cycle-boundary subset exists
closest_priors: SSTRAC skeleton repair under missing poses
candidates.why_it_matters: Real multi-person tracks are rarely uniformly sampled after occlusion and filtering; treating timestamps and missingness as part of the signal model may separate true tempo changes from tracker-induced sampling artifacts.

candidates.name: Identity-Private Switching Oscillator Filter
build_steps: Encode each observed pose into a complex motion likelihood and a periodic-versus-background likelihood, preserving timestamp deltas and joint masks.
For each identity, maintain a posterior over phase, angular frequency, frequency derivative, periodicity state, and uncertainty; advance it with the actual timestamp delta.
Implement a shared bank of slow, medium, fast, accelerating, decelerating, and pause dynamics, and mix their transition kernels using a window-local soft gate.
Update each identity posterior with a differentiable extended Kalman or sigma-point filter; missing observations trigger prediction-only steps and explicit variance growth.

Train the observation encoder and shared dynamics with masked pose prediction, resampling-equivariant phase increments, forward-backward smoothing consistency, and cross-window state consistency, without per-person count or period targets.

Decode a count from posterior mass crossing successive integer phase boundaries while periodicity is active; use half-open track boundaries, require hysteresis around state transitions, and report expected count plus a credible interval.
candidates.hypothesis: A continuous identity-private phase state with shared switching tempo dynamics will bridge adjacent windows and short occlusions more reliably than independently decoded window responses, especially when people accelerate, pause, and resume at different rates.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Freeze source-video-disjoint MultiRep train/development/test sets and run first with supplied tracks. Tune transition noise and credible-interval thresholds only on development; apply preregistered piecewise warps and gaps to test after the checkpoint is frozen.
comparisons: Independent local-window tempo without carried state
Response-peak decoder using the same encoder
diagnostics: Acceleration-deceleration-pause-resume warps
Occlusions from 0.25 to 1.5 cycles
Identity-state reset at artificial track fragments
Phase, frequency, mode probabilities, variance, and integer-crossing plots
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.evaluation: Three seeds; MRAC metrics, count-interval calibration, post-gap phase error, and paired clustered confidence intervals.

success: At least 10% relative AvgMAE improvement over independent local windows on acceleration-pause-resume clips.
Post-gap median phase error below 0.35 rad for gaps no longer than 0.5 local cycles.
Nominal 90% count intervals achieve 85%-95% empirical video-level coverage with mean width at most 2.0 counts.
Pause segments produce fewer than 0.05 false counts per second.
failure: Switching dynamics improve AvgMAE by less than 3% over a single-dynamics oscillator.
More than 10% of pause segments accumulate at least one false cycle.
Posterior frequency collapses to a tempo extreme in more than 5% of tracks.
Uncertainty intervals miss coverage by more than 15 percentage points or have mean width above 3.5 counts.

candidates.risk: Self-supervised oscillator learning can converge to half- or double-frequency modes, and filtering assumptions may be violated by nonperiodic pose changes or tracker switches.

engineer_gpu_effort.engineering: High: differentiable filtering, stable circular-state updates, switching transitions, and calibration; approximately 5-7 engineer-weeks.
engineer_gpu_effort.gpu: Moderate: sequential filtering limits throughput; approximately 400-800 GPU-hours for three seeds and ablations.

unavailable_inputs: Leakage-free MultiRep split and checksums
Reliable timestamps and per-joint masks
A development-only cycle-timing subset for diagnosing phase without using it as a counting target
Predicted-track artifacts with ID-switch metadata for later robustness evaluation
closest_priors: Classical phase-locked loops and switching oscillator state-space models
candidates.why_it_matters: Counting is fundamentally phase accumulation. Maintaining an explicit private phase clock per identity offers a measurable way to distinguish genuine tempo drift, pauses, and missing observations from window-boundary artifacts.

candidates.name: Overlap-Graph Phase Synchronization
build_steps: Let any shared local-window backbone predict a complex unit phasor, periodicity amplitude, response, and confidence for each identity window.
For every pair of overlapping windows on the same track, estimate a relative phase offset from confidence-weighted masked samples and record its circular uncertainty.
Construct a per-track overlap graph and solve a weighted U(1) phase-synchronization problem for one offset per window, fixing only a single arbitrary gauge.
Reject or downweight inconsistent overlap edges using cycle-consistency residuals, without connecting different identities.
Rotate window outputs by the solved offsets and synthesize one response through normalized overlap-add using only valid observed support.
Decode peaks or integer phase crossings once on the fused track; assign exact seam crossings with half-open intervals and suppress boundary peaks lacking support on both sides.
candidates.hypothesis: Explicitly solving the otherwise arbitrary phase gauge of local windows will reduce duplicate and missed repetitions at overlaps, especially when tempo changes near a window boundary or masks make adjacent window estimates disagree.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Use a frozen source-video-disjoint MultiRep split and supplied tracks. This module is trained or tuned only on train/development outputs from one fixed local-window backbone; test window predictions are generated once from the frozen checkpoint.
comparisons: Global graph synchronization without uncertainty weighting
Graph synchronization with cross-identity edges as a negative control
diagnostics: Shift window grids by 0, 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 hop sizes
Place synthetic tempo changes and missing segments at overlap centers and seams
Report circular edge residuals, graph connectivity, seam-adjacent peak errors, and count variance across grid shifts
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.evaluation: Three backbone seeds; standard MRAC metrics plus seam false-positive/false-negative rates and grid-shift count variance.

success: At least 40% reduction in seam-adjacent duplicate or missed peaks relative to unaligned normalized overlap-add.
Count standard deviation across the four window-grid shifts below 0.15 per track and at least 30% lower than the unaligned method.
At least 5% relative AvgMAE improvement over window-count summation.
Median high-confidence overlap residual below 0.20 rad.
failure: Seam-error reduction below 10%.
Global synchronization changes more than 2% of counts on constant-tempo, fully observed control tracks.
Graph disconnection or low effective overlap affects more than 10% of tracks.
Aligned reconstruction worsens AvgMAE by more than 2% relative to unaligned normalized overlap-add.

candidates.risk: If local phasors are not identifiable or overlap is too sparse, synchronization cannot recover a consistent phase; harmonic disagreements can create apparently consistent but wrong offsets.

engineer_gpu_effort.engineering: Medium: circular estimators, sparse graph solve, and seam-focused tests; approximately 2-4 engineer-weeks.
engineer_gpu_effort.gpu: Low: mostly post-processing and light differentiable training; approximately 100-250 GPU-hours including backbone reruns.

unavailable_inputs: Window-level complex response outputs from an implemented local-tempo backbone
Leakage-free MultiRep split and supplied tracks
Cycle-boundary annotations for seam diagnostics if not available; otherwise synthetic seam placement must be used
Exact valid-support masks after pose preprocessing
closest_priors: Rethinking Temporal Self-Similarity action-start response decoding
candidates.why_it_matters: A local model can predict the right tempo yet still count incorrectly because each window chooses an arbitrary phase origin. Phase synchronization isolates and directly tests that reconstruction failure mode.

candidates.name: Mask-Adaptive Multitaper Tempo Posterior
build_steps: Construct three to five DPSS tapers per local window and re-orthogonalize them under the actual confidence mask so missing samples do not silently destroy the taper geometry.
Compute complex spectra for pose-motion channels under every taper and aggregate them into a log-tempo posterior; retain cross-taper dispersion as estimator uncertainty.
Use posterior band mass and uncertainty to softly route windows to shared tempo-specialized response experts, while each identity retains its own temporal state.
Train with masked reconstruction, temporal-resampling consistency, agreement between independent taper subsets, and entropy regularization that prevents routing solely from uncertainty.
Fuse expert responses with taper-variance-weighted normalized overlap-add and estimate count uncertainty by propagating taper subsets or posterior samples through the decoder.
At boundaries, evaluate only peaks whose complete decoder neighborhood intersects valid support; use asymmetric normalization near track ends and a fixed half-open convention.
candidates.hypothesis: Multitaper spectral estimation will reduce frequency leakage and harmonic instability in short pose windows, while cross-taper dispersion supplies a practical uncertainty signal for routing and count calibration.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Freeze a source-video-disjoint MultiRep split with supplied tracks. Select taper count, time-bandwidth product, and calibration mapping on development only; evaluate all seeds on the same untouched test predictions.
diagnostics: Tempo near frequency-bin boundaries
Short windows containing 1.5-4 cycles
Joint dropout and edge-truncated actions
Reliability diagrams for frequency and count uncertainty
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.evaluation: Three seeds; standard MRAC metrics, expected calibration error, interval coverage, spectral concentration, and boundary-specific count error.

success: At least 20% reduction in local-period median absolute error on bin-boundary synthetic warps relative to Hann STFT.
At least 5% relative AvgMAE and 1.5 absolute Period-mAP improvement over single-taper routing.
Count uncertainty expected calibration error below 0.08 and 90% interval coverage between 85% and 95%.
Track-edge count error at least 25% lower than symmetric zero-padded decoding.
failure: Multitaper improves local-period error by less than 5%.
Cross-taper variance has Spearman correlation below 0.2 with absolute count error.
Mask re-orthogonalization becomes numerically unstable in more than 1% of windows.
Inference cost exceeds 2.5 times the single-taper model without meeting the AvgMAE threshold.

candidates.risk: Taper dispersion measures estimator variability rather than model misspecification; short repetition windows may not contain enough cycles for the theoretical leakage advantage to appear.

engineer_gpu_effort.engineering: Medium-high: batched masked taper construction, uncertainty propagation, and calibration; approximately 3-5 engineer-weeks.
engineer_gpu_effort.gpu: Moderate-high because each taper multiplies spectral and expert evaluations; approximately 400-750 GPU-hours.

unavailable_inputs: Leakage-free MultiRep release, checksums, and source grouping
Pose confidences and timestamps
A protocol-sanctioned development subset for calibration
Compute profile of the eventual shared encoder and experts
closest_priors: Runia et al. 2018 temporal frequency analysis
candidates.why_it_matters: Short local windows create spectral leakage exactly where rapid tempo adaptation is needed. Multitaper estimates can make routing less sensitive to arbitrary window placement and attach testable uncertainty to the resulting count.

candidates.name: Variational Monotone Phase Clock with Pose Reconstruction
build_steps: From each masked local pose window, produce a coarse log-frequency likelihood using a shared time-frequency encoder.

Represent instantaneous log-frequency as a cubic spline over physical time and integrate its softplus-transformed value to obtain a monotone phase clock; include a periodicity gate so background and pauses do not accumulate phase.

Fit the phase clock by minimizing confidence-weighted reconstruction of pose-motion channels with a small harmonic basis in phase coordinates, plus curvature regularization, overlap phase consistency, and known time-warp equivariance.
Infer a Laplace or low-rank Gaussian approximation around spline coefficients to obtain frequency and phase uncertainty.
Route phase-normalized window features to shared response experts, align their clocks in overlaps, and reconstruct one identity response using uncertainty-weighted normalized overlap-add.

Decode integer phase crossings only where periodicity support is active and phase variance is below threshold; treat the left boundary as closed and right boundary as open, and report unresolved boundary mass as count uncertainty.
candidates.hypothesis: Estimating a smooth monotone phase coordinate from masked pose reconstruction will convert acceleration and deceleration into approximately stationary phase-domain patterns, allowing shared experts to model repetition shape without confusing tempo drift with action appearance.

minimum_leakage_free_pilot.data: Use a frozen, checksummed, source-video-disjoint MultiRep split with supplied tracks. Fit all spline, regularization, and uncertainty hyperparameters on development only; apply preregistered piecewise warps to untouched test tracks.
comparisons: Monotone phase clock without pose reconstruction
diagnostics: Linear, quadratic, and abrupt piecewise tempo changes
Pause-resume segments
Harmonic limb motions with different amplitudes
Plots of reconstructed pose signal, instantaneous period, phase uncertainty, periodicity gate, and integer crossings
minimum_leakage_free_pilot.evaluation: Three seeds; MRAC metrics, phase monotonicity violations, reconstruction error, crossing stability, and paired video-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals.

success: At least 10% relative AvgMAE improvement over track-global constant-frequency phase on piecewise warps.
At least 25% lower count degradation under quadratic acceleration than piecewise-constant local period.
Fewer than 0.1% negative phase increments outside declared pauses.
Integer-crossing count changes on fewer than 5% of tracks when the window grid is shifted by half a hop.
failure: Pose reconstruction improves while AvgMAE changes by less than 3%, indicating that the learned clock is not count-relevant.
More than 10% of periodic tracks lock to half or double frequency on harmonic diagnostics.
Uncertainty-gated decoding leaves more than 0.5 expected unresolved cycles per track on average.
Spline optimization fails to converge or produces invalid values in more than 1% of windows.

candidates.risk: Pose reconstruction may favor the strongest limb harmonic rather than the semantic repetition cycle; strict monotonicity can mishandle reversals, irregular subactions, and long pauses.

engineer_gpu_effort.engineering: High: differentiable spline integration, harmonic reconstruction, posterior approximation, and robust crossing logic; approximately 5-7 engineer-weeks.
engineer_gpu_effort.gpu: Moderate-high due to iterative or amortized variational inference; approximately 500-900 GPU-hours.

unavailable_inputs: Leakage-free MultiRep release and canonical-source metadata
Pose channels with confidence masks and physical timestamps
Development-only timing diagnostics for identifying harmonic locking
A verified response decoder and metric implementation
closest_priors: Dynamic time warping and continuous phase estimation
Runia et al. 2018 nonstationary repetition analysis
candidates.why_it_matters: A phase coordinate provides a direct bridge between nonstationary signal analysis and integer counting: it exposes when tempo estimates are smooth, uncertain, harmonically wrong, or unsafe to decode at track boundaries.
